paragraphs.text: Sleep researchers have long known that teenagers' body clocks shift later during puberty, making it difficult for them to fall asleep before 11 pm.
When schools begin at 8 am or earlier, many teenagers are therefore chronically short of sleep. Surveys suggest that most get less than the recommended eight to ten hours on school nights.
The consequences go beyond tiredness in class. Lack of sleep has been linked to poorer mental health, more car accidents among young drivers and lower exam results.
Despite this, changing school hours is difficult. Bus timetables, parents' working hours and after-school sports all depend on the existing schedule.
